body.p: File conflicts happen when users modify the same file on different branches and try to integrate one into the other. File conflicts can occur during a merge, rebase, cherry-pick or revert operation.
To resolve a file conflict, on Git Staging, follow these steps:

ol.li:
Open the file in the Compare Editor to view the differences between the local and incoming version.
On Unstaged files, double-click the conflicted file. Alternatively, right-click the file to open the context menu and choose Open in compare editor.

Choose which changes to keep or discard. You can do this from the Compare Editor or, if the resolution is clear
To stage the file, select Apply.
The contextual menu of a resource also includes Resolve using Mine, Resolve using Theirs, and Mark as resolved.
If you use the compare editor, after you close it, the file is staged automatically and moved to the Staged files area.

body.p: When a conflict is in progress, the Git Staging view shows a state label (for example, Merging...) and the available actions for the current operation, such as Abort Merge and Restart Merge above the file list.
During a merge, the conflict panel remains visible even after all conflicts are resolved and staged, so you can still abort or restart the merge before committing.
